known_issues.summary: One insufficient Event Aligner event invalidates its complete request group and discards otherwise valid sibling mappings.
known_issues.impact: If any target event has fewer than two mapped providers, group validation raises before returning any indexed result. After bounded retries the checkpoint marks every conversation in the group failed, so unrelated events that already have valid two-provider mappings cannot reach event-level ASR or later review.
known_issues.source: Independent PD-056 review on 2026-09-22: an adversarial two-event response with a valid R2 mapping and a one-provider R4 mapping raises `Event Aligner mapped fewer than two providers`; `_run_event_alignment` persists only complete-group results and `_run_asr` then sees no validated mapping for either event.
known_issues.next_action: Separate response-schema validation from per-event sufficiency. Persist valid event mappings and explicit failure reasons independently, retry only the failed request group for transport/schema failures, and add a regression proving one bad event does not block valid sibling events or conversations.
known_issues.resolution: Structured-response violations still retry only their request group, but a well-formed event with fewer than two mapped providers now persists alignment_error=fewer_than_two_providers at event scope. Valid sibling events remain available for clipping and event-level ASR. Independent re-review verified a mixed R2-valid/R4-insufficient regression and traced independent downstream handling in `_run_asr`.

known_issues.summary: Event Aligner validation does not prove that selected anonymous speakers are customer speakers.
known_issues.impact: For a single target event, turns from an Agent speaker can satisfy real-ID, provider-count, overlap and order checks and be cut as customer audio. With multiple targets, the validator only requires a consistent speaker label, so consistently selecting the Agent speaker is also accepted.
known_issues.source: Independent PD-056 review on 2026-09-22: `_validate_event_alignment_group` accepted two real turn IDs whose speakers were both explicitly labelled AGENT. The implementation checks speaker consistency but has no independently derived provider speaker-role ownership to compare against the required customer role.
known_issues.next_action: Add an auditable speaker-role mapping or equivalent deterministic ownership evidence and reject selected turns unless their provider speaker is validated as customer; cover both single-target and consistently-wrong multi-target responses.
known_issues.resolution: The frozen Event Aligner contract now returns an auditable customer_speaker and non-empty disjoint robot_speakers mapping for every provider. The server verifies every role label exists in that provider's real turn catalog and marks any target turn outside the declared customer speaker as selected_non_customer_speaker at event scope. Independent adversarial re-review verified provider coverage, real-label membership, customer/robot disjointness and wrong-Agent-turn isolation.

known_issues.summary: Event-clip preparation failures persist only the exception class and discard the actionable alignment or validation reason.
known_issues.impact: EV-20260922-6AA1 shows the same provider_error/ValueError for R6 and R7 even though R6 lacks two-provider semantic alignment while R7 forms a 60 ms consensus that cannot satisfy the signal validator. The product cannot explain the failure or guide a targeted correction from persisted evidence.
known_issues.source: Read-only production inspection on 2026-09-22 UTC: all three event-provider rows for 1030000000086502 R6 and 1030000000089001 R7 contain only message=ValueError with attempts=0; replaying the persisted full-call results exposes distinct underlying reasons.
known_issues.next_action: Persist a safe event-level preparation error code and actionable message before copying it to provider rows, while retaining per-provider alignment failures in the trace; add regressions for no-consensus and too-short-consensus failures.
known_issues.resolution: Event-clip failures now persist bounded event_alignment_failed or user_signal_validation_failed categories with actionable messages, while successful traces retain selected provider turn IDs, excluded providers and union boundaries. Deterministic regressions cover missing mappings and the production-derived R6/R7/R13 cases.

known_issues.summary: Per-provider short-text scoring can reject the correct ordered customer turn even when the provider timeline contains the matching audio interval.
known_issues.impact: For 1030000000086502 R6, ElevenLabs aligns 'Two two one' at 26.70-27.22s, while Soniox returns the overlapping '2 2 1' at 26.91-27.39s but fails selection because the worksheet says 'Two to. One.' and a stray earlier customer token creates multiple low-similarity candidates. Speechmatics omits the English turn, leaving only one accepted provider and no clip.
known_issues.source: Read-only production replay of EV-20260922-6AA1 on 2026-09-22 UTC using the persisted three-provider full-call results and the deployed alignment implementation.
known_issues.next_action: Resolve Q-016, then replace the per-provider short-text gate with the confirmed whole-conversation event-to-segment mapping contract and add this R6 evidence as a deterministic regression.
known_issues.resolution: PD-056 replaces rule-based target selection with a dedicated Event Aligner over complete conversations. The model may select only existing provider turn IDs; deterministic validation enforces complete membership, provider coverage, order, unique turns and consistent customer speakers. The R6 regression proves 'Two two one' and '2 2 1' map without text normalization deciding the event.

known_issues.summary: Using the strict provider intersection as both consensus proof and final clip core can create an impossible or onset-truncated short-utterance boundary.
known_issues.impact: For 1030000000089001 R7, ElevenLabs returns 18.94-20.48s and Soniox returns a single 19.05-19.11s digit; their 60 ms intersection can never satisfy the validator's 120 ms active-signal minimum, so the clip fails despite two-provider agreement. For R13, the three-provider intersection is 45.57-45.78s although provider onsets range from 45.10 to 45.57s; refinement can extend only 180 ms before that core, producing 45.38-46.03s and trimming the start of the short utterance.
known_issues.source: Read-only production replay and persisted source_clip traces for EV-20260922-6AA1 on 2026-09-22 UTC. Full-call and pure-user waveforms correlate at zero offset (0.967 for 1030000000089001), ruling out a recording timeline shift.
known_issues.next_action: Separate interval agreement from final boundary selection: retain overlap as consensus evidence, but derive an onset-preserving provider-supported envelope and let pure-user activity within the bounded margin refine both edges; reject only after applying a duration-aware rule. Add R7 and R13 regressions.
known_issues.resolution: Overlap is retained only as cross-provider agreement evidence. The final boundary is now the union of the largest unique overlapping provider-turn set, and pure-user signal processing may expand but cannot contract that union. Production-derived regressions resolve R7 to 18.86-20.48s and R13 to 45.10-45.87s.

known_issues.summary: Completed paid full-call transcriptions that fail the new usable-diarization check are retried but never entered in the cost ledger.
known_issues.impact: A provider can successfully transcribe the complete recording yet return one speaker or otherwise unusable diarization. The runner then releases the reservation, retries up to three paid calls and records zero ASR cost, understating spend and weakening the hard budget stop.
known_issues.source: Independent PD-053 re-review on 2026-09-21: an isolated run with three completed one-speaker provider responses made three calls, persisted attempts=3/failed, released all reservations, and returned an empty ASR cost ledger.
known_issues.next_action: Settle estimated ASR cost for every completed provider transcription before applying the diarization usability gate, with an attempt-scoped ledger identity; add a regression proving three unusable completed responses remain charged and bounded by budget.
known_issues.resolution: Every completed full-call provider response now settles its attempt-scoped frozen-rate cost before diarization usability is checked. Three completed one-speaker responses remain three charged calls while the context checkpoint fails after the bounded third attempt.

known_issues.summary: Three-provider interval clustering can merge mutually conflicting ranges through one broad provider and return boundaries outside any common overlap.
known_issues.impact: For target intervals A=2.0-6.0s, B=2.0-4.0s and C=4.1-6.0s, B and C do not overlap, yet all three are accepted as one cluster and the returned interval is 2.0-6.0s. This hides competing two-provider interpretations instead of failing closed and can include audio not supported by the provider consensus.
known_issues.source: Independent PD-053 adversarial trace on 2026-09-21 against align_customer_event using three distinct diarized provider results.
known_issues.next_action: Build consensus from a non-empty common intersection (or explicitly select one uniquely winning subset), reject tied incompatible subsets, derive returned bounds from the accepted consensus, and add a three-provider bridging-conflict regression.
known_issues.resolution: Consensus now enumerates distinct-provider subsets, requires a non-empty common intersection, chooses only one uniquely largest agreeing subset, derives clip bounds from that common intersection, and rejects the three-provider bridge conflict in a deterministic regression.

known_issues.summary: A resumed batch reuses any completed full-call ASR checkpoint without verifying that it was produced under the new speaker-timestamp diarization contract.
known_issues.impact: Batches with pre-PD-053 completed Soniox or Speechmatics context rows can remain permanently unable to form two-provider consensus: retries skip those rows, event clips fail closed, and the same stale context is reused again after every restart.
known_issues.source: Independent PD-053 review on 2026-09-21: EvaluationRunner._run_asr returns immediately for every completed evaluation_asr_runs row before checking result.diarization_contract or usable speaker labels.
known_issues.next_action: Treat completed context rows as reusable only when they satisfy speaker_timestamps_v1 and contain a usable diarized timeline; otherwise create an explicit migration/retry path with preserved accounting and add a restart regression using legacy completed rows.
known_issues.resolution: Full-call checkpoints are now reusable only when they carry speaker_timestamps_v1 and a valid timestamped timeline containing at least two speakers. Legacy or malformed completed rows are re-requested with monotonic attempt numbering and a versioned reservation/cost identity; a restart regression proves replacement before event clipping.

known_issues.summary: The new interval clustering can label non-overlapping ranges, or duplicate results from one provider, as the required two-provider consensus.
known_issues.impact: Two ranges separated by up to 0.75 seconds are accepted and their median endpoints can produce a clip interval covered by neither provider; two rows carrying the same provider name also satisfy the count of two. This violates PD-053's overlapping, multi-provider fail-closed contract and can select the wrong user audio.
known_issues.source: Independent PD-053 deterministic trace on 2026-09-21: Soniox 4.0-4.5s plus Speechmatics 5.0-5.5s returned a 4.5-5.0s consensus, and two Soniox rows returned consensus_providers=['soniox','soniox'].
known_issues.next_action: Require distinct provider identities and a non-empty common overlap before accepting a cluster, derive the interval from that overlap (with any tolerance explicitly specified), and add regressions for gapped and duplicate-provider inputs.
known_issues.resolution: Alignment now rejects missing or duplicate provider identities and accepts only intervals with an actual overlap. Deterministic regressions cover both duplicate-provider and nearby-but-gapped evidence.

known_issues.summary: Grouped LLM attempts are persisted only when a group completes or exhausts all three attempts, so process recovery after a billable intermediate schema failure can still reuse an old attempt identity.
known_issues.impact: If the worker restarts after attempt 1 or 2 was charged and recorded but before the group reaches a terminal checkpoint, the resumed provider call can collide with the existing reservation/ledger key and be omitted from cost accounting.
known_issues.source: Independent recovery trace on 2026-09-21: _llm_json records usage before parsing structured JSON, but the Pass 1/Pass 2 group rows keep status=pending and attempts=0 until final success or third failure. Resume derives the next attempt only from that stale group row.
known_issues.next_action: Persist the latest external attempt after every settled call/schema failure or recover it from durable per-group usage telemetry, then add a process-restart-after-attempt-1 regression for both grouped passes.
known_issues.resolution: Pass 1 and Pass 2 now checkpoint pending status with the cumulative attempt number after every intermediate exception. Resume treats any persisted attempt as a retry, adds correction guidance, and starts at the next unique attempt; regressions assert attempts 1 through 6 across two executions.

known_issues.summary: The exact Pass 1 minimum-group branch-and-bound can take exponential time for a 56-conversation batch that does not fit in one or two groups.
known_issues.impact: A Qwen-sized batch can appear stuck before any external job is created, replacing avoidable request over-splitting with an unbounded planning delay.
known_issues.source: Independent deterministic stress check on 2026-09-21: 56 non-symmetric PassOneUnit inputs (seed 4, estimated input 1500-4500, 1-4 user events) under context=100000, max_output=50000 and margin=1000 exceeded a 2-second local planning deadline. The search has no aggregate lower-bound pruning before trying to disprove a two-bin solution.
known_issues.next_action: Add admissible group-count lower bounds and bounded exact-search pruning that preserves PD-045's minimum-group guarantee, plus a 56-conversation performance regression.
known_issues.resolution: The exact search now computes admissible total-context and output-cap lower bounds before branching and prunes with remaining aggregate capacity. The independent 56-conversation seed-4 case returns the proven three-group plan in under one millisecond locally and is retained as a regression.

known_issues.summary: Pass 1 Gemini execution disables Thinking with thinking_budget=0 for every Gemini model, including Gemini 3.x models whose verified control is thinking_level.
known_issues.impact: A newly grouped Gemini 3.8 Flash Pass 1 request can be rejected by the provider before producing any structured result, so the intended production-job reliability fix is not yet safe to release.
known_issues.source: Independent static review on 2026-09-21: src/llm/capabilities.py records Gemini 3.8 Flash as thinking_level=low, while EvaluationRunner._llm_json builds ThinkingConfig(thinking_budget=0) whenever disable_thinking is true. Current Pass 1 tests mock _llm_json and do not exercise the provider request config.
known_issues.next_action: Use the verified per-model Gemini capability when minimizing Pass 1 reasoning, retain thinking_budget=0 only for models that support it, and add request-shape regressions for Gemini 2.5 and Gemini 3.8 without making an external call.
known_issues.resolution: Evaluation now resolves the verified Gemini capability per model: Gemini 3.8 Flash uses thinking_level=low while budget-capable models retain thinking_budget=0. A native configuration regression covers Gemini 3.8 without an external call.

known_issues.summary: A user-triggered retry of a failed Pass 1 or Pass 2 group reuses attempt numbers 1-3 and therefore reuses cost-reservation and ledger idempotency keys from the previous execution.
known_issues.impact: The retried provider request can incur real cost while INSERT OR IGNORE retains the old ledger row, understating spend and weakening the hard-budget guarantee.
known_issues.source: Independent execution trace on 2026-09-21: both grouped retry loops restart range(1, 4), while _llm_json derives reserve and cost keys only from batch, stage, group and attempt. Focused retry tests mock _llm_json and therefore do not exercise budget/ledger persistence.
known_issues.next_action: Persist a cumulative or run-qualified attempt identity for every new external request, keep provider/group membership stable separately, and add a retry-after-failure cost-ledger regression for Pass 1 and Pass 2.
known_issues.resolution: Grouped Pass 1 and Pass 2 persist the cumulative attempt after every failed external try, including intermediate schema failures, and resume from that count after process or user retry. Every later paid request therefore receives a fresh reservation and cost-ledger identity while frozen group membership remains unchanged; regressions assert attempts 1 through 6 across two executions.

known_issues.summary: Pass 1 dynamic packing uses a best-fit-decreasing heuristic that can create more request groups than the confirmed minimum-safe-group contract allows.
known_issues.impact: Some batches make avoidable paid LLM requests and the implementation does not satisfy PD-045's exact request-count behavior.
known_issues.source: Independent deterministic counterexample on 2026-09-21: token sizes 1000,1000,1000,1500,3000,3500 under context=11000, max_output=10000 and margin=1000 are packed into 3 groups by the implementation although a safe 2-group arrangement exists.
known_issues.next_action: Use an exact bounded packing strategy for the supported batch size or define and confirm an explicit approximation contract; add the counterexample as a regression.
known_issues.resolution: Pass 1 packing now uses deterministic exact branch-and-bound after a best-fit upper bound, with symmetric aggregate-state pruning. The independent counterexample is locked as a regression and produces the required two groups.

known_issues.summary: Production Gemini and earlier Qwen structured-output jobs can repeat the same schema failure across all application retries.

known_issues.summary: Pure-user ASR clip boundaries can be materially wrong when the workbook time column is treated as speech onset and the next event is outside the audio timeline.
known_issues.impact: For 1030000000086502 R10, the source timestamp is 60.254s while detectable user speech is approximately 57.77-59.38s. The current event-start-to-next-event-start rule begins after the utterance and, because R11 is 119.255s while the audio ends at 117.38s, produces an approximately 57.13-second clip instead of the short user sentence. Provider transcripts from that clip are not valid evidence for R10.
known_issues.source: Read-only inspection of the committed source workbook and WAV plus the production clipping implementation on 2026-09-21. The source audit already records decreasing/out-of-audio timing as warnings, but prepare_case_asr_clip blocks only MP3/WAV duration mismatch and clamps the invalid next-event boundary to audio duration.
known_issues.next_action: Define and implement an onset-aware pure-user boundary derivation using the user WAV signal and neighboring speaker events, reject ambiguous clips before provider dispatch, and add this conversation as a regression fixture.
known_issues.resolution: PD-048/PD-049 replace the invalid row-to-next-row interval with anchor-guided speech-island detection on the pure-user WAV, reuse the resulting exact source interval for provider input/playback/Benchmark, and add a separate once-per-conversation/provider full-call context checkpoint. Independent review exposed that a louder earlier utterance distorted the search-wide energy threshold and made real R6 fail; threshold calibration is now local to the anchor and equally close islands fail closed. Local-real inspection resolves R6 to 9.940-10.870s and R10 to 57.580-59.610s; 223 repository tests pass, including loud-earlier-speech and ambiguous-island regressions.

known_issues.summary: Qwen Event Aligner still uses the generic 120-second timeout and has no timeout-triggered group split.
known_issues.impact: The user-initiated retry of EV-20260923-E65A reached Event Aligner after ASR, but its single 36-conversation group carried an estimated 789,893 input tokens and reserved up to 101,888 output tokens, then timed out three times at 120 seconds. All 36 alignment rows failed, 239 Case-provider projections became unavailable, and the retry never reached Pass 2.
known_issues.source: Read-only production SQLite, service log and executor inspection on 2026-09-22 Pacific time. The failed EAG0001 group contains 36 conversations with estimated_input_tokens=789893, reserved_output_tokens=101888 and attempts=3/error=timeout. The earlier 22-conversation EAG0001 completed once with 548,511 estimated input tokens and 50,496 reserved output tokens. The packer admits the larger request because Qwen3.8 is modeled with a one-million-token context and optimizes for the fewest groups; it also reserves the payload twice because the rendered system prompt and user message both contain it. _llm_request_timeout grants Qwen 180 seconds only for pass_1 and 300 seconds only for pass_2, leaving event_alignment at 120 seconds despite disable_thinking=true. PD-068 then externally proved the proposed direction: the same 36-conversation work planned into seven <=64K groups, and the fullest 3-conversation/10-event group completed in 22.947 seconds with valid mappings, zero reasoning tokens and USD 0.021239 estimated cost.
known_issues.next_action: Stop optimizing Event Aligner only for the fewest context-valid groups: remove avoidable payload duplication, add a latency-aware per-group input/output ceiling, deterministically split large groups, and give the remaining bounded Qwen request an explicit timeout before retrying E65A.
known_issues.resolution: PD-069 applies the shared 64K final-input/32K output envelope to the exact deduplicated wire request, disables Thinking, uses 180 seconds, pre-splits an oversized single conversation by stable target-event subsets, supersedes and bisects timeout/schema-failed multi-conversation parents, bounds singleton leaves to one extra attempt, and merges durable subset results by event ID. Deterministic packing, timeout-policy and restart-safe checkpoint tests pass.

known_issues.summary: Mass Event Aligner fallout writes Case-provider failures concurrently and can lock SQLite, masking the real provider failure.
known_issues.impact: After the Event Aligner timeout, 239 projection failures were scheduled through one unbounded asyncio.gather. Independent SQLite connections contended and raised database is locked, so E65A ended with a generic OperationalError instead of the actionable alignment-timeout cause.
known_issues.source: Read-only production service log at 2026-09-23T05:48Z traces sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked from _run_asr.project -> checkpoint_result while persisting evaluation_case_asr_runs.
known_issues.next_action: Serialize or batch projection checkpoint writes and set a bounded busy timeout/transaction strategy; preserve the upstream Event Aligner failure as the batch-level cause.
known_issues.resolution: Case/provider projections are now assembled without database writes and committed through checkpoint_case_asr_results_bulk in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction with PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000. A 240-row regression passes without lock amplification.

known_issues.summary: A live-request elapsed timer can flash 00:00 after each polling render before the next one-second timer tick.
known_issues.impact: The displayed duration appears to reset for one frame even though the underlying started_at is stable, making a healthy wait look discontinuous.
known_issues.source: Frontend runtime inspection: activeOperationRows recreates every time element with literal 00:00, while refreshVisibleElapsedTimes runs only on the independent one-second interval.
known_issues.next_action: Render the elapsed value directly from started_at and refresh it immediately after every polling render, retaining the one-second interval for subsequent ticks.
known_issues.resolution: activeOperationRows now computes the initial MM:SS value from started_at before inserting the row; the one-second updater continues from the same durable timestamp. Desktop and narrow Chromium verify a 65-second request renders as 01:05+ without a 00:00 frame.

known_issues.summary: Each Multi-ASR live row shows the global cross-provider ordinal and total instead of that provider's local progress.
known_issues.impact: When 36 conversations are sent to each of three providers, Soniox, Speechmatics and ElevenLabs rows each display a denominator of 108 even though each provider owns 36 jobs; only the stage-level aggregate should use 108.

known_issues.next_action: Persist provider-local ordinal/total for each active row while keeping the stage summary as the aggregate across providers.

known_issues.summary: Event Aligner Qwen requests are rendered inside the Multi-ASR stage instead of a distinct post-ASR alignment stage.
known_issues.impact: Operators reasonably interpret waiting qwen under Multi-ASR as an unexpected transcription request. Event Aligner is actually an LLM prerequisite between full-call ASR and Pass 2, but the top-level batch stage remains evaluation_asr and the five-card UI has no alignment card.
known_issues.source: Production screenshot and executor/UI inspection: _run_asr invokes _run_event_alignment while the batch stage is evaluation_asr; the active operation is tagged event_alignment but active rows are injected into the current top-level card.
known_issues.next_action: Expose Event Alignment as an explicit stage between Multi-ASR and Pass 2, or define it as a clearly named substage within the fourth card after product confirmation.
known_issues.resolution: PD-067/PD-069 add event_alignment as the fourth durable stage and render six cards. Qwen Align operations appear only under Event Alignment; Multi-ASR contains provider work only. Desktop and narrow Chromium regressions pass without horizontal overflow.

known_issues.summary: The monthly-batch summary shows only the currently active source package, and historical batches do not freeze a dataset identity.

However, activating the 82-conversation package replaced the shared source index; a paused or retryable 56-conversation batch can therefore resolve source conversations through the current 82-conversation dataset instead of its original package, and historical source-detail links are not reliably batch-scoped.
known_issues.source: Read-only production inspection on 2026-09-23 found immutable upload directories containing 56 and 82 workbooks, four retained 56-conversation batch rows, active dataset 0801-0831.zip with 82 conversations, and a shared source index containing only 82 rows. Code inspection shows import_dataset_upload calls _sync_source_data, which deletes and replaces evaluation_source_conversations, summary reads fixture_status for only the active package, and create_batch stores source counts/name but no dataset_id used for subsequent source resolution.
known_issues.next_action: Define the card as retained unique source inventory (138 for the current two packages), persist a dataset registry, freeze dataset_id on every batch, scope conversation/event lookup and retries to that dataset, and migrate existing 56/82 batches to their retained package before allowing old-batch retries.

known_issues.summary: A post-PD-069 E65A retry reaches Pass 2 but aborts while registering a regrouped request whose idempotency key already belongs to an older group ID.

The latest traceback at 2026-09-23T08:05:46+00:00 is sqlite3.IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed: evaluation_pass2_groups.batch_id, evaluation_pass2_groups.idempotency_key from checkpoint_pass2_group. known_issues.next_action: Resolve prior Pass 2 groups by idempotency key as well as group ID, reuse the canonical persisted group when exact membership matches, reject only true membership drift, and add a production-derived regression covering retry after partial Event Alignment availability changes. Do not ask the user to retry E65A again until this correction is independently verified and deployed.
known_issues.resolution: Pass 2 now reconciles planned groups against the persisted idempotency key, reuses the canonical group ID only when exact Case membership matches, and rejects true group-ID or membership drift. The E65A-derived ordinal-change retry regression passes.

known_issues.summary: Event Alignment materialization is conversation-atomic, so one missing target mapping can discard valid sibling event mappings and make their Case audio appear unavailable.
known_issues.impact: For E65A conversation 1030000000070676, R28 received valid mappings from all three providers and its independently finalized Benchmark clip is a valid 4.55-second 8 kHz mono PCM WAV, but the current evaluation_case_asr_runs rows for R28 still have no clip path and report event_alignment_failed. R30 genuinely lacks two-provider consensus, yet its failure causes the conversation-level alignment checkpoint to remain failed and prevents R28's valid mapping from being returned to clip preparation.
known_issues.source: Read-only production SQLite and audio inspection on 2026-09-23. Source history places R28 at 134.151s, R29 at 136.799s and R30 at 136.588s, so R30 is out of order. ElevenLabs and Soniox merge customer speech from approximately 133.6-137.1s into one turn; only Speechmatics exposes a later S3 customer segment around 137.33-137.77s. The completed bounded Align result maps R28 through all three providers but marks R30 fewer_than_two_providers. _run_event_alignment only checkpoints and returns a conversation when the merged event-ID set exactly equals the current target set, so partial valid mappings are not materialized.
known_issues.next_action: Replace conversation-atomic materialization with audio-island Case materialization under PD-070. Persist valid Cases independently, merge multiple adjacent source events when they map to one speech island while retaining all source event IDs, and allow valid sibling Cases to continue. Add regressions for both the two-island R28/R30 pattern and a true many-events-to-one-island pattern.
known_issues.resolution: Audio-first Case materialization is persisted independently per frozen speech island. Adjacent historical events assigned to one island are retained as source_event_ids on one Case, and an ambiguous or failed Case no longer rolls back valid siblings or blocks their Pass 2 evidence.

known_issues.summary: Case audio positioning is text/ASR-turn-first even though the pure-user waveform provides the more reliable event boundary signal.
known_issues.impact: A wrong or merged LLM turn mapping becomes the authoritative clip interval. The waveform stage may only validate and expand that interval, so it cannot split two distinct user utterances or correct a text-driven boundary. This can merge adjacent Cases, make a valid short Case unavailable, contaminate playback/Benchmark audio, and propagate the wrong evidence into Pass 2 across the whole evaluation set rather than one exceptional Case.
known_issues.source: Production-derived audio-only inspection for 1030000000070676 found two distinct user-track activity islands at 133.60-136.70s and 137.36-137.72s without reading transcript text. The current R28 Benchmark interval is 133.42-137.97s and therefore merges both islands. Code inspection confirms prepare_case_asr_clip first derives an interval from LLM-selected full-call ASR turns; _validate_and_refine_user_interval then explicitly refuses to contract the provider union and can only validate or expand it.
known_issues.next_action: Implement PD-070 as a full audio-first positioning redesign: derive stable speech islands from user_record, monotonically assign them to ordered customer events using timestamps only as soft anchors, merge adjacent events assigned to one island into one traceable Case, persist success/failure per Case, and project full-call provider turn text afterward by temporal overlap without allowing text to move audio boundaries. Define composite Case identity, minimum-duration, interval-gap and migration contracts before coding and cover the complete dataset with deterministic boundary regressions. Keep KI-190's independent Pass 2 idempotency-key recovery correction in the same delivery scope.
known_issues.resolution: The runtime now freezes pure-user waveform islands first, uses historical event order as the hard constraint, excludes historical timestamps, normalizes number/spelling forms only to rank legal paths, and projects provider turns after the boundary is frozen. Boundary determinism and 223/two two three regressions pass.

known_issues.summary: Evaluation reports do not expose historical Turn annotation errors as a distinct data-quality metric and evidence list.
known_issues.impact: Audio-first evaluation can discover over-split, wrongly merged or misordered historical Turns, but the current runtime has no separate review queue, confirmed count, affected-row count or drill-down. Operators therefore cannot validate the source-data conclusion and may misread an automatic candidate as an ASR vendor error.
known_issues.source: Product-owner requirements PD-071 and PD-074 on 2026-09-23. Current report schemas and frontend Case tables expose ASR decisions, evidence, labels and exclusions but no historical-turn anomaly review, metric or affected-event trace.
known_issues.next_action: After renewed V1.20 User Gate 1, implement the dedicated Turn anomaly review queue and immutable confirm/reject decision, then freeze confirmed historical_turn_error_group_count, affected_historical_turn_count and Turn review coverage; add group-first details, source IDs, audio evidence, partial/preliminary/final report behavior and export coverage while keeping the data-quality metrics independent from ASR error rates and Benchmark ingestion.
known_issues.resolution: A separate Turn anomaly queue now supports audio playback, confirm, reject and deferred-open review. Immutable reports include only confirmed group count, affected Turn-row count, review coverage and group-first evidence; these values remain separate from ASR rates and Benchmark ingestion. Desktop and narrow regressions pass.

known_issues.summary: One persisted Event Alignment singleton exhausted its bounded retry with a structure error and is not yet covered by the confirmed controlled-LLM migration contract.
known_issues.impact: Retiring the all-conversation LLM Event Aligner does not by itself define what happens to legacy failed Align checkpoints. A retry could remain blocked by the old singleton failure or accidentally dispatch the retired request shape unless migration first rebuilds audio-first evidence and allows the controlled LLM only for a newly detected ambiguous Case.
known_issues.source: Production-derived E65A inspection discussed with the product owner on 2026-09-23 found one Event Alignment group already reduced to a single conversation but still exhausted by invalid structured output. The current PD-069 implementation persists exhausted singleton leaves; the initial PD-070 task list did not name this historical checkpoint migration separately.
known_issues.next_action: Under the confirmed Q-019 policy, keep the failed singleton row as immutable historical diagnostics, exclude it from direct retry eligibility, rebuild the affected conversation's Case/provider evidence through the deterministic audio-first path, and permit only the newly defined controlled LLM fallback if the rebuilt Case remains ambiguous. Add regressions proving the legacy failure cannot block valid sibling Cases or Pass 2 and cannot silently replay the retired request shape.
known_issues.resolution: The audio-first path never invokes the legacy Event Aligner. Failed singleton rows remain unchanged for diagnostics while new per-Case evidence is rebuilt; a regression proves the retired request cannot replay and does not block two valid sibling Cases. Controlled LLM assistance is invoked only for newly ambiguous audio-first assignments.

known_issues.summary: The initial no-LLM audio-first proposal incorrectly implied that time overlap alone can bind unreliable historical events to audio Cases.
known_issues.impact: Historical event timestamps are unreliable. When event and speech-island counts differ, or text forms such as '223' and 'two two three' are not normalized, order plus time overlap may admit multiple legal mappings. Claiming success would silently attach the wrong historical event to a valid audio boundary and contaminate Pass 2 and the report.
known_issues.source: Product-owner challenge on 2026-09-23: the historical timestamp may not place the historical text at the same audio time as the ASR turn, so the previous example did not prove deterministic alignment. Review of Q-019 confirmed Option A named time overlap but did not define historical-event-to-island disambiguation or the non-unique fallback.
known_issues.next_action: PD-076 froze the V1.20 controlled Option C baseline. Under a subsequent explicit development instruction, implement waveform-first alignment, ambiguity-only batch-frozen LLM assistance and deterministic validation, then complete Checkpoints A/B/C before any release claim.
known_issues.resolution: Option C is implemented: waveform islands and monotonic order define the legal space, text/normalized digits rank but cannot move boundaries, and only non-unique or low-evidence cases can call the batch-frozen LLM. Returned IDs, order, provider ownership and frozen boundaries are deterministically validated.

known_issues.summary: Benchmark uniqueness is batch-scoped, so the same conversation ID and event ID can be stored again by a later batch.
known_issues.impact: Repeated evaluation of the same source event can create multiple Library rows, inflate Benchmark totals and Good/Bad distributions, duplicate exported audio, and leave competing labels for one original event.
known_issues.source: Code review on 2026-09-23: evaluation_benchmarks declares UNIQUE(batch_id, conversation_id, event_id). Both automatic materialization and manual review use INSERT OR IGNORE, so duplicates are suppressed only inside one batch; a different batch ID bypasses the constraint. The existing Benchmark Delta Spec and design also documented the same batch-scoped identity.
known_issues.next_action: Implement PD-073/PD-075 after renewed Gate 1: migrate to a global conversation/event business key, preserve existing canonical samples and their trace evidence, make identical ingestion return the canonical ID, discard later conflicting candidates without a sample/revision/review task, safely reconcile existing duplicates, and add cross-batch plus conflict regressions.
known_issues.resolution: Storage initialization archives later duplicate rows with their revisions, retains the oldest canonical row, and enforces a global conversation/event unique index. Identical later ingestion reuses the canonical ID with trace evidence; conflicting candidates are audit-logged and discarded without changing counts, revisions or exports.

known_issues.summary: The V1.20 audio-first legal-path ranker does not yet use adjacent robot-turn context or explicit cross-provider consistency, and LLM-assisted selections lack the required semantic-conflict check.
known_issues.impact: When event/island counts differ and customer text is weak or tied, the runtime can route a resolvable assignment to LLM/manual review or accept a provider selection whose IDs and ownership are valid but whose texts conflict semantically.
known_issues.source: Independent V1.20 review on 2026-09-23 traced _event_island_score and _resolve_ambiguous_audio_cases against the frozen PD-070 contract.
known_issues.next_action: Retain the new ranking evidence and deterministic post-LLM rejection regressions in the release suite.
known_issues.resolution: Legal-path ranking now persists customer text, digit normalization, adjacent robot context and cross-provider consistency components without moving frozen islands. Strong role, digit or semantic provider conflicts keep a Case ambiguous; the same checks run after an LLM selection, and regressions prove context changes the legal-path choice while conflicting provider digits cannot be overridden.

known_issues.summary: Historical Turn anomaly detection and review evidence are incomplete for the V1.20 contract.
known_issues.impact: Only many-events-to-one-island over-split groups are created. Wrong-merge/order candidates are not classified, and the review UI omits the suggested Case mapping and provider evidence required to make an informed confirmation.
known_issues.source: Independent V1.20 review on 2026-09-23 traced checkpoint_evaluation_case, list_historical_turn_issues and the Turn review renderer against PD-071/PD-074.
known_issues.next_action: Retain all three anomaly classes, exact-island playback and desktop/narrow evidence in the release suite.
known_issues.resolution: The completed conversation checkpoint now groups over-split, wrong-merge and evidence-backed order candidates, persists every suggested Case/island and provider turn, protects completed reviews from retry mutation, and exposes exact-island audio through the review API. The formal review and report DOM render the mapping, provider evidence and playback; backend and desktop/narrow regressions pass.

known_issues.summary: The confirmed historical Turn row metric double-counts a source Turn when overlapping anomaly groups are both confirmed.
known_issues.impact: A source Turn can belong to both a wrong-merge and an order-anomaly group. Summing each group's affected count inflates the report even though the frozen contract requires unique affected source Turn rows.
known_issues.source: Independent V1.20 re-review on 2026-09-23 traced historical_turn_quality against the PD-071 report contract and found that it sums affected_turn_count instead of taking the union of confirmed source event IDs.
known_issues.next_action: Retain the overlapping wrong-merge/order regression in the release suite.
known_issues.resolution: historical_turn_quality now takes the union of (conversation ID, source event ID) pairs across confirmed groups. A regression confirms two overlapping confirmed groups report two unique affected Turn rows rather than the previous summed value of three.

known_issues.summary: A successful Pass 2 retry cannot clear the batch failure state because terminal aggregation counts every historical failed group row.
known_issues.impact: Replacement groups can complete and materialize valid decisions, but the batch returns to partially_failed because the eight original failed groups remain status=failed. Repeated user retries therefore create more paid replacement requests without making the terminal state reachable.
known_issues.source: Read-only production inspection of EV-20260923-E65A on 2026-09-23 showed successful replacement groups followed by partially_failed at 11:51 UTC, then another user retry at 11:52 UTC. executor.py finalization counts every pass2_group_rows row whose status is failed, without excluding replaced historical groups or reconciling current Case coverage.
known_issues.next_action: Make terminal Pass 2 status derive from current canonical Case coverage and active retry lineage, retire or exclude replaced failed groups, and add a repeated-production-retry regression before another E65A retry.
known_issues.resolution: The runner now freezes the current canonical Case keys before Pass 2, filters balancing/final decisions/materialization/reporting to that membership, and derives terminal failure only from missing or failed current Case checkpoints. Historical group failures remain diagnostic and cannot independently force partially_failed. Deterministic regression and the full suite pass without a provider call.

known_issues.summary: Historical Turn wrong-merge detection treats every unassigned audio island as a review candidate without proving that it is an independent spoken Turn.
known_issues.impact: Natural within-Turn pauses or RMS fragmentation create orphan islands that are attached to the nearest historical event and surfaced as wrong_merge. E65A currently shows 137 groups covering 140 unique Turns; 119 groups are wrong_merge, making the review queue impractically large and dominated by likely false positives.
known_issues.source: Read-only E65A inspection on 2026-09-23 found 448 RMS islands, 123 persisted Cases and 137 Turn issue groups: 119 wrong_merge, 16 order_anomaly and 2 over_split. checkpoint_historical_turn_issues labels every orphan island by its nearest assignment; detect_audio_islands splits speech after only 250 ms of inactivity and does not first establish a robot boundary or provider-supported independent customer Turn.
known_issues.next_action: Separate speech fragments from semantic Turns: consolidate islands using audio/provider/robot-boundary evidence, require independent-Turn evidence before wrong_merge, and regenerate review candidates with regression coverage for pauses inside one Turn versus genuine multiple customer Turns.
known_issues.resolution: Wrong-merge generation now suppresses islands crossed by the same provider customer turn and requires either robot-boundary evidence or distinct customer turn IDs from at least two providers. Candidate refresh preserves reviewed evidence and marks disappeared open candidates superseded. Pause-fragment, real-extra-turn and review-state regressions pass.

known_issues.summary: The Manual Review queue tabs remain partly Chinese after switching the formal page to English.
known_issues.impact: English-mode users still see ASR Case 复核 and Turn 异常复核, and the empty Turn queue heading/subtitle also remain Chinese.

known_issues.summary: The initial Turn-candidate refresh deletes reproduced deferred issues and their append-only review revisions.

known_issues.resolution: Candidate reconciliation now leaves reproduced pending/deferred rows in place, appends an auditable superseded transition only for disappeared open candidates, can reactivate a later-reproduced superseded candidate, and never mutates confirmed/rejected rows. The regression proves deferred version 2 survives replay and becomes superseded version 3 with both revisions retained.

known_issues.summary: The live Turn queue title is not re-rendered when the language changes after bootstrap data has replaced its bilingual DOM node.

known_issues.next_action: Re-render historical Turn issues on every language change and extend the desktop/narrow browser regression to assert the dynamic queue heading.
known_issues.resolution: The Turn queue title now keeps the localized label and dynamic count in separate nodes, and the language callback refreshes historical Turn content. Desktop and narrow Chromium both pass English-to-Chinese tab/title/count assertions.

known_issues.summary: The Manual Review page can keep a stale Turn issue count after backend reconciliation has superseded old candidates.
known_issues.impact: The product owner sees 135 Turn issues even though production currently has 40 open groups; the stale count makes the corrected evidence rule appear ineffective and overstates manual workload.

E65A contains 95 superseded wrong_merge rows, 40 current open groups and a preliminary report with 2 confirmed plus 40 pending groups. The frontend reuses runtime.bootstrap review arrays on review navigation unless another action refreshed bootstrap.
known_issues.next_action: Refresh bootstrap before entering Manual Review, opening a batch's review queue, or switching ASR/Turn modes; add a UI contract regression and verify the current production count after deployment.
